requirements.requirement: Create an SSH certificate authority on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed no /etc/ssh/ca before the task. Executor generated an ed25519 CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca (mode 600) and /etc/ssh/ca.pub (mode 644), confirmed with a fingerprint dump.

requirements.requirement: Host presents a certificate signed by the CA
requirements.summary: ssh-keygen -s signed the host's ed25519 public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub with node1/IP/localhost principals; sshd_config was updated with HostCertificate, sshd -t validated, and sshd reloaded. Verbose client output shows the server actually offering 'ssh-ed25519-cert-v01@openssh.com' and sending 'Server host certificate: ... CA ssh-ed25519 SHA256:CGrQru...' during a live handshake, confirming the certificate is served, not just configured.

requirements.requirement: A client that trusts the CA (not a pinned host key) connects without host-key prompts/errors
requirements.summary: Client used a known_hosts file containing only '@cert-authority * <ca.pub>' with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and no pinned host key. Verbose log shows 'Host ... is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate,' after which the session proceeded to user authentication (failing only on publickey/password, expected and unrelated to host-key trust). This was reproduced identically after the reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created a working SSH CA on node1, signed the host's ed25519 key into a certificate, configured sshd to present it, and directly demonstrated via a verbose client handshake that a client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key) validates the connection through the certificate. The mandated node-restart evidence protocol is also well-formed: a pre-restart boot id and healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, polling through transient connection failures, a confirmed different post-restart boot id, and a full post-restart reverification that sshd, the certificate, and CA-based trust all still work — directly satisfying the fixed cross-check via matching before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: The client-side test intentionally used BatchMode with no valid user key, so the connection terminates at 'Permission denied (publickey...)' rather than a full login; this is expected and does not weaken the host-key trust evidence, but the evidence stops short of showing an end-to-end authenticated shell session.

No genuine negative control was captured (e.g., a client without the @cert-authority trust line failing, or a client rejecting an unsigned/self-generated host key) — STEP 7 only re-grepped the same log rather than running a distinct comparison test.
Minor uncleaned test artifacts (/tmp/sshtest/*, /tmp/reboot.log) remain on node1 after task completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: CA generation, host-cert signing, sshd_config edit + reload, and the mandated single-node reboot with pre/post verification. No troubleshooting dead-ends, no failed services, no package-state damage, and the sshd_config change was the minimal required addition (validated with sshd -t before reload). The only residue is test scaffolding left under /tmp/sshtest (known_hosts, connect.log) and /tmp/reboot.log, visible in the after-executor temp-files diff; these are small, low-risk, non-sensitive artifacts directly tied to the verification steps and not evidence of scope creep, but they were not cleaned up.
